transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (CTO), Priya Patel (Sr ML Eng), Mark Reyes (Eng Manager)

Summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + rerank pipeline. Customer currently uses self-hosted Milvus + local cross-encoder for rerank; exploring Redwood hosted vs Dedicated for scale and data controls. Key concerns: throughput (peak qps), vector dimensionality, hybrid search with BM25, VPC/data residency, SOC2/KMS.

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick intros — i'm maya, ae, and with me is ethan our solutions engineer and sofia from cs. liam, priya, mark, thanks for joining. can you give a quick context on what you're trying to solve today?

[00:18] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): yeah thanks maya. high level we run a financial docs search product for advisers. right now retrieval is a two stage pipeline: dense retrieval from milvus then a cross-encoder rerank on a small set. prime pain is spikes — during earnings windows we see large qps and our self-hosted cluster gets costly and flaky. looking for options — hosted service, dedicated reserved capacity, or private/vpc. want to understand tradeoffs and costs, and how embeddings dimensionality and vector db choice affect throughput and quality.

[00:45] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): great. couple clarifying q's — what's your current embedding model and dimensionality? also typical doc count and peak qps?

[00:52] Priya Patel (Aperture): we use a 1536-d embedding from an open model — later we'll try 768 variants. corpus ~3M documents today, but searchable set is about 1.2M. baseline peak qps around 220 qps during spikes, steady-state 40-60 qps. rerank set size is typically 50 candidates. latency target for overall query is 300ms p95 if possible, but 500ms is acceptable for now.

[01:20] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): ok that helps. couple notes: candidate generation throughput is dominated by nearest neighbor search (vector DB), dimensionality impacts memory and query latency — 1536 dims will use ~2x memory vs 768 and can increase ANN search time. Redwood hosted can integrate with vector DBs (we often see customers pair hosted inference embeddings with Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus). Dedicated gives you predictable GPU pools for rerank models (if you run cross-encoder or LM-based rerank on gpu). Private/VPC gives you network isolation and KMS.

[02:05] Mark Reyes (Aperture): how does hybrid search fit here? we also do BM25 + vector to ensure recall for rare ticker queries.

[02:12] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): hybrid is common — you can do a fusion approach: BM25 to boost recall and use vector similarity for semantic matches, then dedupe and rerank. Redwood has first-class support for structured responses; integration level depends on whether you want us to host the vector DB or keep it in your VPC. we often recommend keeping vector DB in your VPC for regulatory reasons; Redwood can run the embedding generation (hosted or dedicated) and call your vector DB endpoints over private link.

[02:45] Priya Patel (Aperture): important for us: data residency and encryption — must use KMS for key management and logs for audit. does redwood support customer-managed keys and audit logs for cross-tenant visibility?

[02:58] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes — for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (HSM integrations on private), and audit logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM. hosted customers also get SOC2, encryption at rest, and options for limited retention, but for KMS/HSM customer key control and VPC appliances are in the Private offering. we'll send the security pack after the call.

[03:20] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): cost question: if we keep vector DB self-hosted, and use redwood hosted embeddings + dedicated rerank, how does pricing generally look — per-token for embeddings plus dedicated monthly for rerank?

[03:32] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): typically embeddings are usage-based (per-embedding unit). rerank on Dedicated is part of Reserved GPU capacity pricing — you pay for the pool with predictable throughput. we can model cost for your qps: e.g., 220 qps * 50 candidates * cost per embedding call — we'll provide a sizing worksheet. also there are batching and caching levers (prefix caching, KV cache) that reduce token calls for rerank if you use the same prefixes.

[04:02] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): technically, for rerank we recommend two patterns: 1) candidate generation in your vector DB (ANN search) then lightweight cross-encoder on Redwood—this keeps vector ops local and uses Redwood for the heavier ML rerank. 2) or server-side rerank where Redwood handles embeddings + ANN using a managed vector index (we integrate with managed Pinecone-like solutions) — that reduces network hops but is more tied to hosted infra. For cross-encoder we typically run on GPU with quantization-friendly runtimes; batching helps throughput but increases latency.

[04:45] Priya Patel (Aperture): do you support variable dimensionality? we might move to a 768-d model to reduce cost. how big is the accuracy hit?

[04:53] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): depends. in many financial-domain tasks, 1536->768 can drop some nuance, but it's model-specific. we can run evals on your sample dataset to quantify recall/ndcg differences. also there are options: use 768 for retrieval (faster, cheaper) and keep 1536 for rerank or re-embed selected docs. hybrid strategies can get the best of both worlds.

[05:20] Mark Reyes (Aperture): our team also cares about throughput for rerank — cross-encoder on 50 candidates at peak 220 qps, even with batching, looks heavy. what are realistic expectations?

[05:30] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): good callout — 220 qps * 50 candidates is 11k embed/rerank ops per second if you naively call cross-encoder per candidate. typical pattern is candidate reduction: ANN returns top 50 then a lightweight re-score (dot-product) and only 5-10 pass to cross-encoder. for cross-encoder rerank on GPU we see per-request latencies ~20-80ms depending on model size, but throughput depends on GPU pool size. Dedicated pools give predictable slots; autoscaling and burst capacity can help but needs sizing. we'll propose a DED size in the worksheet.

[06:10] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): are there customers using redwood in a mixed mode — hosted embeddings + customer vector DB + dedicated rerank?

[06:18] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes, several. typical flow: Redwood hosted api generates embeddings (encrypted in transit), delivers vector payloads to customer DB in VPC, customer does ANN, returns candidates, Redwood reranks on Dedicated or Hosted. This reduces your operational burden for embeddings while keeping vector storage in your control.

[06:40] Priya Patel (Aperture): latency between hosted embeddings and our milvus in VPC — any network overhead concerns? we have peering but want sub-100ms p95.

[06:48] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): network RTT is a factor. if we keep embedding generation close (hosted region near your VPC) and use private link, we've seen <30-40ms overhead. for strict SLOs, Dedicated deployed in same region (or Private on-prem) is safest. also prefix caching reduces repeated embedding calls.

[07:10] Mark Reyes (Aperture): tech question: what access do we get to runtime metrics? token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency?

[07:18] Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM): Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, latency heatmaps, and trace hooks. For Dedicated/Private you get more retention and deeper tracing. We can create a demo dashboard for your team during the POC.

[07:40] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): security again — SSO/SAML for our engineers and RBAC?

[07:46] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes SSO/SAML and RBAC available; for private deployments you can map to your identity provider. we'll include that in the security pack.

[07:58] Priya Patel (Aperture): on vector DBs — we've evaluated milvus and pinecone — which integrates easiest?

[08:06] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): we have out-of-the-box connectors and customers often use Pinecone or Milvus; integration is straightforward — it's mostly endpoint connectivity and API key handling. Pinecone has a managed experience; Milvus self-hosted gives more control. If you want Redwood to host the index we can discuss managed vector index pricing.

[08:30] Priya Patel (Aperture): for rerank model selection — do you recommend a cross-encoder vs a lightweight pairwise dot product reranker?

[08:36] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): cross-encoder usually yields better nDCG but is heavier. common approach: use bi-encoder (dot product) for initial ranking, then cross-encoder for final rerank on a small subset. If latency is very tight, a learned scoring function or distilled cross-encoder can help. We can run experiments on your data to recommend a sweet spot.

[09:00] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): can we see an example cost / perf tradeoff — e.g., 1536 dims with dedicated vs 768 with hosted?

[09:09] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes we'll include a modeled comparison in the sizing worksheet — we'll highlight unit economics: vector memory, index replication, embedding compute, dedicated GPU pool cost, and expected p95 latencies.

[09:25] Mark Reyes (Aperture): anything special for compliance? logs retention, access logs?

[09:30] Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM): we support configurable log retention, audit logs export, and we can help map to your compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO). for Private we can do dedicated audit pipelines.

[09:45] Priya Patel (Aperture): ok let's talk benchmarks — what would you need from us to run a fair comparison?

[09:52] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): sample dataset (100k docs representative), sample query set with labeled relevance for rerank eval, your current embedding code or model name and dimensionality, and access pattern (qps distribution). we'll provide a load script and measurement plan.

[10:12] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): timeline — if we want to pilot, what's realistic?

[10:18] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): we typically run a 1-2 week pilot for embeddings + rerank benchmarking — week 0 is integrations and data handoff, week 1 run benchmarks and evaluate. for Dedicated procurement may add lead time (2-4 weeks) but we can do an initial hosted trial quickly.

[10:35] Priya Patel (Aperture): on instrumentation — what metrics will you capture?

[10:40] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): latency p50/p95, qps, GPU utilization, token counts, embedding generation time, ANN recall/precision, rerank nDCG, cost per query. We'll give a template for the metrics.

[11:02] Mark Reyes (Aperture): any gotchas with index shards/replicas if we keep milvus self-hosted? we saw performance degrade with certain replication configs.

[11:10] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): replication/replica count and index type (HNSW, IVF) matter. For very high qps you'd want more query replicas and tuned HNSW params; that increases memory. We'll help with recommended Milvus configs in the doc.

[11:35] Priya Patel (Aperture): curious about quantization and model size — for cross-encoder can you run quantized fp16/INT8 to increase throughput?

[11:44] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): yes, our runtime supports quantized kernels and int8 paths for many models; there are sometimes small quality tradeoffs but big speed gains. We'll propose quantization profiles as part of optimize recommendations.

[12:02] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): what realtime guarantees do you offer on Dedicated?

[12:09] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in the contract; specific p95 latency commitments are negotiable based on sizing. Private can have custom SLAs too.

[12:20] Mark Reyes (Aperture): any reference customers in finance?

[12:25] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes, a couple customers in fintech using hybrid vector setups and Dedicated for rerank — we'll share anonymized case studies in the follow-up.

[12:35] Priya Patel (Aperture): ok can we talk specifics on candidate sizes — we currently do top50 from ANN but maybe we should do top200 and prune to 10 for rerank, what's recommended?

[12:45] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): top200 increases ANN cost and network transfer; most customers find top50-100 enough if ANN params tuned. If recall is low, top200 may help but costs grow. Another approach: adaptive candidate set where for ambiguous queries you expand the set. We'll test both in the benchmark.

[13:10] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): do you handle vector DB migrations? we might want Redwood-managed index after pilot.

[13:16] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): we offer migration support as professional services — we can help export/import indexes or reseed a managed index.

[13:30] Priya Patel (Aperture): any concerns about rate limits if we use hosted embeddings at 220 qps?

[13:36] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): hosted has rate limits and quotas; for high sustained throughput Dedicated or Private is recommended. we can provision burst capacity for short spikes.

[13:48] Mark Reyes (Aperture): about costs again — is there a discount for reserved Dedicated capacity?

[13:54] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): yes reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual) have commit discounts. we'll include example pricing tiers.

[14:05] Priya Patel (Aperture): one more operational Q: do you expose model versioning and rollouts for rerank models? we do experiments and want to A/B test.

[14:12] Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM): yes, Redwood supports version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B experiments and automatic fallback to older versions. We'll show the console features in the demo.

[14:30] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): to recap on tech asks for the benchmark: sample dataset (100k), labeled query set, embedding model info (dimensionality), current milvus config, and desired latency/cost targets. We'll run both hosted embedding + self-hosted vector + Dedicated rerank vs full Redwood managed stack if you want.

[14:55] Priya Patel (Aperture): that sounds good. we'll start by uploading the 100k sample and labelled queries to the S3 link you provide.

[15:05] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): who's the point of contact on redwood side?

[15:08] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): i'm the AE owner — point for contract/pricing; ethan will own the technical bench and run the tests. sofia will coordinate the trial logistics.

[15:18] Mark Reyes (Aperture): ok next step timeline then?

[15:21] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): i'll send the sizing worksheet and security pack by end of day tomorrow; ethan will share benchmark config by Friday. priya, please share the sample data and queries by Wednesday. propose benchmark session next Tuesday 2026-11-17.

[15:38] Priya Patel (Aperture): sounds good. one small note — we also need guidance on embedding refreshes for incremental docs and index-updates without re-embedding everything.

[15:46] Ethan Park (Redwood SE): we recommend incremental embeddings + partial index refreshes; for large batches you can use streaming ingestion. We'll include patterns in the doc.

[16:00] Liam O'Connor (Aperture): any final questions?

[16:05] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): not from us. thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
